name: Barzillai the Gileadite
charge: Bringing beds, wheat, and honey to the king and his hungry men in the wilderness at Mahanaim
summary: When David fled from Absalom, an old man of Rogelim brought provision for the king and the people with him, saying, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness. David wanted to keep him at court for life. Barzillai was eighty and asked only to die in his own city; David took his son instead, and charged Solomon on his deathbed to remember the house.
offense: When David came to Mahanaim during Absalom's rebellion, Barzillai joined Shobi and Machir in bringing beds, vessels, grain, pulses, honey, butter, sheep, and cheese for the people. They considered the people hungry, weary, and thirsty in the wilderness (2 Samuel 17:27-29). Their service answered the actual condition of those who had fled. Barzillai was very aged and a very great man, and he sustained the king while David lay at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 19:32). Wealth became provision at a moment when the kingdom's outcome was not settled. He assisted the displaced king before the victory made that assistance safe or fashionable. After the rebellion, he came down to conduct David over Jordan. David offered to take him to Jerusalem and feed him there. Barzillai, eighty years old, answered concerning the limits of his age and asked to return to his own city near the burial place of his father and mother (2 Samuel 19:31-37). His service had not been a concealed demand for life at court.
judgment: The king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem. Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee. And the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him. David to Solomon: shew kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table: for so they came to me when I fled because of Absalom thy brother. Centuries later his family was still known by his name.

Barzillai was very aged and a very great man, and he sustained the king while David lay at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 19:32). Wealth became provision at a moment when the kingdom's outcome was not settled. He assisted the displaced king before the victory made that assistance safe or fashionable.

After the rebellion, he came down to conduct David over Jordan. David offered to take him to Jerusalem and feed him there. entries.commentary: Ahithophel had already given Absalom wicked counsel in the previous chapter, telling him to go in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel so that the hands of all that were with him would be made strong. Ahithophel was David's own counselor turned traitor, being the devil the Bible speaks of, working deceit and betrayal from inside the gates of Israel. His counsel in those days was regarded as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God. That tells you Ahithophel was very influential and had the gift of gab, so persuasive that his advice sounded almost biblical. Now he asks Absalom to let him choose out twelve thousand men to pursue David that same night while David was weary and weak handed, to smite the king only and bring back all the people. He wanted the victory and the bragging rights of being the one who killed King David.

Absalom wanted a second opinion, so he called Hushai the Archite to hear likewise what he would say. There is safety in a multitude of counselors, but only where the counsel is according to thus saith the Lord; a counselor who does not go to the scriptures is not one you should want. Hushai told Absalom that Ahithophel's counsel was not good at this time. He reminded him that his father and his mighty men were mighty and chafed in their minds as a bear robbed of her whelps, war ready and strategic, and that David would not lodge with the people but move by night. Hushai warned that if Absalom's men were overthrown at the first, even the most valiant warrior whose heart is as the heart of a lion would utterly melt, for all Israel knew David was a mighty man. This shows David and his mighty men were on another level; none of Absalom's thousands could compare to them. Instead Hushai counseled that all Israel be gathered from Dan to Beersheba as the sand by the sea, with Absalom going to battle in his own person. This deliberately inaccurate counsel would waste time gathering troops and give David room to escape; Hushai was a counterintelligence agent, a spy planted in righteousness, always siding with King David. Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

Hushai reported both Ahithophel's counsel and his own to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, telling them to send quickly and warn David not to lodge in the plains of the wilderness that night but to pass over speedily, lest he be swallowed up. The messengers Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited by En-rogel; a maidservant carried the word to them, but a lad saw them and told Absalom. The Most High put His spirit on certain people to orchestrate His plan; often when a man tries to do evil to another, it falls back on him, for he that diggeth a pit shall fall therein. They fled to a man's house in Bahurim that had a well, and a woman spread a covering over the well's mouth and ground corn upon it to camouflage it. When Absalom's servants came asking, she told them the men had gone over the brook of water, and the pursuers returned to Jerusalem. The two came up out of the well and told David to arise and pass quickly over the water. David and all the people passed over Jordan by the morning light, and there lacked not one of them that was not gone over.

When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he set his house in order and hanged himself. The evil counsel he devised reared its head around and bit its author; evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid. To be righteous is to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord; all unrighteousness is sin, and sin is the transgression of the law. David was righteous and did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while the sinner was pursued by his own evil.

The victory that day was turned into mourning for all the people, because they heard how the king grieved for his son, and they got them by stealth into the city as ashamed men steal away when they flee in battle. Joab came into the house and told David he had shamed the faces of all his servants who had saved his life and the lives of his sons, daughters, wives, and concubines, because he loved his enemies and hated his friends. Joab said if Absalom had lived and all of them had died, it would have pleased David well. No one else could speak to the king this way, but Joab knew David's skeletons. Joab charged David to arise and speak comfortably unto his servants, swearing that if he did not, not one man would tarry with him that night, and that would be worse than all the evil that had befallen him from his youth. Then the king arose and sat in the gate, and all the people came before him.

All the tribes of Israel were at strife, saying the king had saved them from the Philistines and their enemies but had fled the land because of Absalom, who was now dead, so why did they say nothing about bringing the king back. David sent to Zadok and Abiathar the priests to speak to the elders of Judah, asking why they were the last to bring the king back when they were his brethren, his bone and his flesh. He told Amasa that he would make him captain of the host in the room of Joab. David bowed the heart of all the men of Judah as the heart of one man, so they sent word for him to return with all his servants, and the king came again to Jordan while Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and conduct him over.

Shimei the son of Gera the Benjamite hastened down with a thousand men of Benjamin, along with Ziba the servant of Saul's house with his sons and servants, and fell down before the king at Jordan. Shimei begged the king not to impute iniquity unto him nor remember the day he did perversely when David went out of Jerusalem, confessing that he had sinned. This was the same Shimei who had cursed David, cast stones, and called him a bloody man and a man of Belial while David was in a low state surrounded by his mighty men. Abishai and the sons of Zeruiah said Shimei should be put to death for cursing the Lord's anointed, but David rebuked them as adversaries, asking whether any man should be put to death that day in Israel when he knew he was king. He swore Shimei would not die. David understood grace long before the New Testament, for grace has always been around.

Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, having neither dressed his feet, trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes from the day the king departed until he returned in peace, showing his mourning for David. When asked why he had not gone with the king, Mephibosheth said his servant Ziba had deceived him and slandered him, since Mephibosheth was lame and could not saddle his own beast. He acknowledged that all his father's house were dead men before the king, yet David had set him to eat at his own table, so he had no further right to cry to the king. David told him to speak no more of the matter and said that he and Ziba should divide the land. Mephibosheth answered that Ziba could take it all, for it was enough that his lord the king had come again in peace to his own house.

Barzillai the Gileadite, a very aged man of fourscore years, came down from Rogelim to conduct the king over Jordan, having provided the king with sustenance at Mahanaim, for he was a very great man. When David invited him to come and be fed in Jerusalem, Barzillai asked how long he had to live that he should go up, saying at eighty years old he could no longer discern the taste of what he ate or drank nor hear the voice of singing men and women, so he would only go a little way over and asked to return and die in his own city by his parents' grave. He sent Chimham in his place, and the king kissed and blessed Barzillai, who returned to his own place. A quarrel then arose between the men of Israel and the men of Judah over who had the right to bring the king back. Judah claimed the king was near of kin to them, being of the tribe of Judah, while Israel claimed ten parts in the king and more right in David, and the words of Judah were fiercer than the words of Israel. This was the tribe strife that would later split the northern and southern kingdoms, though they were all Israel.

The days of David draw near that he should die, and he charges Solomon to be strong, to keep the charge of the Lord his God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his statutes, commandments, and judgments as written in the law of Moses, that he may prosper. There was a stipulation for the throne to continue: if his children take heed to their way and walk before the Most High in truth with all their heart, the throne stands. Reading through the kings, we see many who broke the commandments, and among their children some were righteous and some unrighteous. -
Solomon thrusts out Abiathar from being priest unto the Lord, fulfilling the word the Most High spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh. The old judgment on Eli's line is carried out.

Joab, who had turned after Adonijah, flees to the tabernacle of the Lord and catches hold of the horns of the altar, but Solomon sends Benaiah to fall upon him. Joab dies for the innocent blood he shed when he slew Abner and Amasa, two men more righteous and better than he, without David's knowledge. The blood returns upon Joab's own head and upon his seed, while upon David and his seed and throne there shall be peace forever from the Lord. Benaiah is set over the host in his place.

Shimei is commanded to build a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, never crossing the brook Kidron on pain of death, and he agrees. After three years he goes to Gath after his runaway servants and breaks the oath, so Solomon has Benaiah put him to death, and the kingdom is established in Solomon's hand.

These are the children of the province who came up out of captivity, whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away, returning each man to his own city in Jerusalem and Judah. The first wave came led by Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, and the other chief men. Zerubbabel had been one of the bodyguards of the Persian Empire, the wisest guard granted a request in 1 Esdras. -
The men of the people of Israel are numbered family by family, house by house, showing exactly who returned. The record is precise because Israel kept careful count of who came back to the land.
The priests, Levites, singers, porters, Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants are all counted. Each service group is named so the temple work could be carried out by the proper lineages.

Some could not show their father's house or their seed, whether they were of Israel, and were set aside. The priests who could not find their register by genealogy were put from the priesthood as polluted, forbidden the most holy things until a priest stood up with Urim and Thummim. -
The whole congregation together numbered 42,360, beside their servants and maids. Their singing men and women, horses, mules, camels, and asses are all counted.

Some of the chief of the fathers, coming to the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, offer freely to set it up in its place. They give after their ability to the treasure of the work, and the priests, Levites, and people dwell in their cities.

Five were wise and five were foolish. The foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them; the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. The oil is the wisdom of the scriptures. The foolish come afterward saying, Lord, Lord, open to us, and are answered, Verily I say unto you, I know you not. Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord.

Every man received according to his several ability, and the two who traded were told, Well done, thou good and faithful servant. The one who hid his talent blamed his lord and called him a hard man, and was answered, Thou wicked and slothful servant. That fearful spirit is not of the Most High, and a man should examine himself for it. Unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance; but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath. Knowledge that is not used is knowledge that is lost.

He separates them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats, and says to those on the right hand, Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Meeting the need of a brother or sister in the body is counted as done to Christ himself. Those on the left hand are answered with the same measure: inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

verses.text: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo–debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched pulse,
And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.
And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.
And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?

I am this day fourscore years old: and can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?
Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?

Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.
And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
But shew kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table: for so they came to me when I fled because of Absalom thy brother.

And of the children of the priests: the children of Habaiah, the children of Koz, the children of Barzillai; which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name:
Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:
For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:
Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.
Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink?
When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee?
Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
